What is an AI agent marketplace?

An AI agent marketplace is a directory of pre-built AI agents that automate specific business workflows — lead qualification, customer support triage, invoice processing, content creation, and hundreds of other tasks. Instead of designing an AI employee from scratch, you pick a template that matches the job you want done, connect your apps, and deploy it in minutes.

Arahi's marketplace has 226 templates across sales, marketing, customer support, operations, finance, and HR — every one fully editable after deployment, running on 1,500+ native integrations, no code required. Need something custom? Build your own agent once you see the pattern.

Frequently asked questions

An AI agent marketplace is a directory of pre-built AI agents that automate specific business workflows — lead qualification, customer support triage, invoice processing, content creation, and hundreds of other tasks. Instead of designing an agent from scratch, you pick a template that matches the job you want done, connect your apps, and deploy it in minutes.

Zapier and n8n templates are deterministic, step-by-step workflows that fire only on a specific trigger and run the same actions every time. Arahi's marketplace templates are AI agents — they reason about each input, decide which steps to take, can branch, retry, or escalate, and adapt their behavior to your instructions in plain English. You can still trigger them on events, but they're built to handle messy, real-world inputs (free-text emails, ambiguous tickets, unstructured data) that rule-based workflows fail on.

Every template in the marketplace is available on all Arahi plans, including the Starter plan. The Starter plan ($49/month) includes 1,000 actions per month, access to all 226 templates, and 1,500+ native integrations. Higher tiers unlock more execution volume, priority processing, advanced models, and team collaboration.

Yes — every template is fully editable after deployment. You can rewrite the agent's instructions in plain English, change which apps it connects to, modify trigger conditions, add or remove steps, and tune its decision criteria. Most teams start from a template, run it for a few days, then adjust based on what they learn.

No. Every template deploys without code. You authenticate the apps you want the agent to use via one-click OAuth, optionally edit the agent's natural-language instructions, and activate it. If you can write a Slack message describing what you want the agent to do, you can deploy and customize a template.

Most templates go live in under 5 minutes. The time is split between connecting the apps the agent needs (usually 2–3 OAuth approvals), reviewing the default instructions, and activating the agent. More complex agents (multi-step pipelines with custom logic) may take 15–30 minutes if you want to tailor every step before going live.
